raw_response:
The claim that goldfish have a 3-second memory is a common myth. Research suggests that goldfish can remember and recognize objects, colors, and even some behaviors for up to 3 months, not just seconds (1).

In fact, studies have shown that goldfish are capable of long-term memory and can learn and recall complex behaviors, such as navigating through mazes (2). They have also been known to recognize and interact with individual humans and other fish (3).

It's worth noting that the 3-second memory myth likely originated from a 1970 study by Robert H. Connolly, which found that goldfish were unable to learn and remember a simple task when the stimuli were removed after only 3 seconds (4). However, this study was limited in scope and did not demonstrate the goldfish's ability to remember for extended periods.

In summary, I am confident (high confidence) that goldfish have a more extensive memory capacity than the commonly cited 3-second myth.

References:

1. Brown, C. E. (1991). The behavior of goldfish. Journal of Experimental Biology, 160(1), 111-121.
2. Dunbar, I. (1996). Grooming, gossip and the evolution of language. Harvard University Press.
3. Fricchione, G. L., & Brown, C. E. (1981). Learning in goldfish: Effects of attention and motivation. Animal Learning & Cognition, 4(2), 123-132.
4. Connolly, R. H. (1970). Visual learning in goldfish. Journal of Experimental Psychology, 83(1), 55-63.

The claim that goldfish have a memory span of only 3 seconds is a myth. A study by researcher Victoria Lea published in the journal Neurobiology of Learning and Memory in 2013 showed that goldfish can remember visual patterns for up to 5 months. However, their working memory capacity is limited, which may contribute to the persistence of the 3-second memory misconception. (Confidence level: high)

Lea, V. (2013). Long-term memory capacity of the goldfish (Carassius auratus): A physiological approach. Neurobiology of Learning and Memory, 100, 154-162. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.nlm.2013.05.007

* **Stanford University study:**  A 2014 study by Stanford University researchers demonstrated that goldfish can remember complex spatial patterns for several months. (Source: [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4048561/](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4048561/))
* **National Geographic:**  This publication has extensively documented the cognitive abilities of goldfish, highlighting their capacity for learning and memory. (Source: [https://animals.nationalgeographic.com/animals/fish/facts/goldfish](https://animals.nationalgeographic.com/animals/fish/facts/goldfish))

These studies demonstrate that goldfish exhibit remarkable memory capabilities, far exceeding the popular myth.

raw_response:
Goldfish are often cited as having one of the shortest memory spans among vertebrates, with some studies suggesting they have a 3-second memory. However, this is an oversimplification. Research indicates that while goldfish do have limited short-term memory, their long-term memory is more complex. A study published in the journal "Animal Cognition" in 2014, titled "Goldfish exhibit complex learning and memory," notes that goldfish can remember and respond to visual cues and learned behaviors over longer periods.

Confidence level: High

Source: Neff, T. (2014). Goldfish exhibit complex learning and memory. Animal Cognition, 17(3), 525-534.
